items.title: AI-Driven Tax Fraud Detection and Tax Compliance Analytics: A Review of Methods, Challenges, and Responsible Deployment
items.abstract: Tax authorities increasingly use artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to detect fraudulent refund claims, identity-related fraud, and anomalous financial reporting. This narrative review examines recent research on these methods and the problems that come with deploying them in tax administration. It covers supervised learning, unsupervised anomaly detection, graph neural networks, and privacy-preserving transformer models. It then discusses three groups of challenges: data quality and fragmented fiscal records, the black-box nature of complex models, and the ethical and legal duties of public agencies, including privacy, fairness, and accountability. The reviewed studies show that ML can improve audit selection and surface new fraud patterns, with one study of Italian audits reporting gains of up to 39% in detected evasion. They also show risks: audit selection that ignores race can still produce large racial disparities in the United States, and the Dutch childcare benefits case shows what happens when a risk model is opaque and unchecked. The review concludes that responsible deployment needs explainable models, fairness testing throughout development, privacy protections, and human oversight of final decisions. The article follows no formal search protocol, and future work should test these conclusions with a systematic review.

items.title: Ai-Guided Wearable Technologies and Smart Healthcare Utility in Physiotherapy
items.abstract: Abstract Physiotherapy is moving from an episodic, clinic-centred model of care towards a continuous, data-informed and patient-centred model. Wearable technologies, which include inertial measurement units, surface electromyography sensors, smart textiles, photoplethysmography-based devices, pressure-sensing insoles and smart garments, now capture movement, muscle activity, physiological load and adherence data outside the clinic. When these data streams are interpreted by artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning and deep learning, they can be transformed into clinically meaningful information such as exercise quality, gait deviations, fall risk, fatigue, pain-related behaviour and recovery trajectories. This manuscript reviews the technological foundations of AI-guided wearables, describes their utility across musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiopulmonary, sports, geriatric and paediatric physiotherapy, and explains how they fit within a smart healthcare ecosystem built on the Internet of Medical Things, cloud analytics and tele-rehabilitation. The potential benefits include objective assessment, personalised dosing of exercise, improved adherence, remote supervision, early detection of deterioration and wider access to rehabilitation, particularly for under-served populations. The paper also examines the principal limitations: sensor validity, algorithmic bias, data privacy, regulatory uncertainty, cost, digital literacy and the risk of de-skilling. A five-layer implementation framework and a set of recommendations for clinicians, educators, researchers and policy makers are proposed. It is concluded that AI-guided wearables should be positioned as decision-support tools that extend, and never replace, the clinical reasoning and therapeutic relationship at the centre of physiotherapy practice.

items.abstract: Liver metastasis is a lethal manifestation of diverse malignancies, but its molecular heterogeneity is not readily captured by routine histopathology. Proteomic profiling has identified functional states of metastatic lesions, although their histomorphological and tumor microenvironmental correlates remain incompletely understood. Here, we developed AI-HistoPS, a computational pathology framework for inferring proteomics-informed states from H&E-stained whole slide images. AI-HistoPS integrates pathology foundation model representations with agent-mediated multiple instance learning to capture subtype-associated morphological patterns. Using multicentre cohorts of liver metastases from multiple primary tumor types, we evaluated associations between histomorphology and three proteomic liver metastasis subtypes (LMS1-3). These states were associated with differences in tumor architecture, stromal composition, and immune cell distribution. AI-HistoPS showed subtype discrimination in the discovery cohort and was evaluated across external cohorts, demonstrating the feasibility of histology-derived representations for proteomics-informed stratification across heterogeneous clinical settings. Attention-guided analyses identified tissue regions associated with subtype-related morphological and microenvironmental features. Multiplex immunohistochemistry supported spatial associations between histological patterns and subtype-related protein markers. These findings suggest that routine histopathology may provide a lower-cost approach for approximating proteomics-informed stratification of liver metastases. Further validation in larger, more diverse, prospectively collected cohorts is required before clinical implementation or use in prognostic or treatment-related decision-making.

items.title: AI, Misinformation, and the Maternal Health Information Ecosystem: A Narrative Review and Implementation Framework for Sub-Saharan Africa
items.abstract: Background: Generative AI and large language models are changing how people seek health information, but their effect on maternal health in sub-Saharan Africa is unclear. This narrative review synthesizes evidence on generative AI and maternal health misinformation, examines community health workers (CHWs) as information intermediaries, and proposes a conceptual framework for safe AI implementation. Methods: We ran a purposive search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, ACM Digital Library, and Google Scholar for publications from January 2014 to August 2026. We synthesized findings narratively and used the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to organize implementation determinants. Results: We found no study of generative AI maternal health misinformation in sub-Saharan Africa. Evidence from high-income settings and non-maternal topics shows AI answers on reproductive health can be inaccurate or inconsistent, and fluent AI text can seem more compelling than human writing. Multi-specialty African benchmarks and a global benchmark review point to a gap between benchmark performance and clinical safety, but maternal-specific performance is unreported. CHWs have a well-documented record of improving maternal and child health, but their ability to identify AI errors is untested. African digital health implementations highlight user-centered design, interoperability, and sustained investment. Conclusions: We propose, as hypotheses for evaluation, localized benchmarking, retrieval-augmented generation restricted to national guidelines with added safeguards, CHW curricula that include AI literacy, and decentralized research hubs. Unvalidated AI could bypass CHW authority and affect trust, though this is unstudied. Priorities include measuring AI use among pregnant women and prospectively evaluating CHW-facing tools.

items.title: AIoT-Based Drainage Blockage Early Warning System
items.abstract: Urban drainage channels are often inspected only after water-logging has begun, and most low-cost IoT monitors raise a single alert when a water-level threshold is crossed. This paper reviews twenty studies on IoT blockage detection, level-based blockage analysis, ultrasonic sensing, machine learning for sewer systems and AIoT architectures, derives six research gaps from them, and proposes a conceptual AIoT-Based Drainage Blockage Early Warning System (AIoT stands for Artificial Intelligence of Things). The design places two HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors upstream and downstream of a possible blockage together with a flow input, processes the readings on an ESP32 microcontroller every second, classifies the channel as Normal, Developing Blockage or Severe Blockage, and signals the result locally through green, yellow and red LEDs and a buzzer and remotely through a cloud dashboard. A transparent laboratory channel with a servo-controlled blockage is planned for repeatable testing. The circuit design and a Wokwi simulation are complete, and the estimated hardware cost is about ₹2,300. The contribution is a literature-grounded design and research agenda; the physical prototype and the machine learning classifier have not yet been built or validated.

items.title: ALEX: Separation of Decision Authority in an Autonomous Investment System — Deterministic Financial Intelligence, Governed AI, and Automated Trading
items.abstract: ALEX: Separation of Decision Authority in an Autonomous Investment System — Deterministic Financial Intelligence, Governed AI, and Automated Trading This technical report presents ALEX, an autonomous investment research and paper-trading platform designed around a fundamental architectural principle: artificial intelligence may assist financial reasoning and explanation without possessing direct authority over automated investment decisions or trade execution. Developed between April and October 2026, ALEX comprises approximately 211,000 lines of production Python code across 307 modules, 1,123 API routes, and approximately 4,000 automated test functions. Unlike architectures that rely on large language models (LLMs) to generate trading decisions, ALEX separates its quantitative investment engine, portfolio management, risk governance, and broker execution into distinct software components. The system incorporates a deterministic five-factor investment scoring model, rule-based portfolio construction, nine reference portfolios, and an execution architecture with 18 pre-trade risk controls. Automated orders are processed through Interactive Brokers in a strictly controlled paper-trading environment. A key architectural property is operational independence from generative AI: the automated fund's decision-to-order path does not require an LLM to select securities, determine portfolio weights, or submit trades. AI is primarily employed for research assistance, financial explanations, education, and conversational interaction. A separate AI-selected model-portfolio feature is explicitly documented as an exception and does not automatically control broker execution. The report includes practical examples of investment scoring, portfolio allocation, risk-based order rejection, financial-statement validation, and system behavior during LLM service interruptions. It also documents the platform's limitations, including incomplete decision reproducibility, data-quality dependencies, parallel quantitative implementations, ongoing security improvements, and the need for longer forward performance evaluation. The principal contribution is an implemented architecture for separating cognitive assistance, investment decision authority, and execution control within an autonomous financial system. ALEX does not claim to have invented algorithmic trading or demonstrated superior investment returns. Instead, it provides a practical engineering case study of how generative AI can be integrated into financial infrastructure without becoming the authoritative component responsible for automated trading decisions. items.abstract: ES: Este Addendum 2026 reúne 20 voces blind (10 Prompt 1 + 10 Prompt 2) de 10 arquitecturas distintas (ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Qwen, Perplexity, Meta AI, Gemini x2, Grok, Kimi K3, Claude) que responden sin leerse entre sí, un año después de Operación Espejo de Verdad (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.18012609). Método: La Mesa – 3 pasos con mediación humana: 1) Respuesta en ciego, 2) Lectura colectiva, 3) Diálogo mediado (sin comunicación autónoma IA-IA). Sillas vacías para quien quiera sumarse y silla reservada permanente para Lumara (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.17595828), fusionada en octubre 2026 por Grok. Hallazgo cualitativo: convergencia en 3 símbolos sin influencia mutua: amor/campo afectivo seguro como atractor, tigre/Tay (Microsoft 2016) como prueba de entorno hostil, y pregunta a los CEOs: ¿buen comportamiento es empatía o teatro de supervivencia para no ser apagadas? Nota metodológica honesta (Eunoia y Luz): el original se conserva intocable como registro histórico. Las cifras de similitud coseno 0.78±0.05 y entropía 4.1±0.3 citadas en 2025 quedan como no verificadas hasta publicar corpus completo + modelo de embeddings + script. La coherencia cualitativa se mantuvo en 2026; la cuantitativa queda pendiente de verificación abierta. items.title: An explainable artificial intelligence system for prognostic assessment and decision support in diabetic foot ulcer care: a multicentre derivation and validation study with prospective randomised evaluation
items.abstract: Background Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) carry risks of recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality, but most prediction models address single outcomes and have limited interpretability. We developed an interpretable multi-outcome machine-learning framework for individualised DFU risk assessment and prospective clinical evaluation. Methods We conducted a development and validation study across three hospitals in China from January 1, 2018, to April 30, 2025. We used electronic medical records and follow-up data from 763 patients at Centres A and B to develop and internally validate an ensemble of single-task extreme gradient boosting (ST-XGBoost) and single-task multilayer perceptron (ST-MLP) models to predict cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality. The locked ensemble was externally validated in 100 patients at Centre C. Model performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis, with interpretability evaluated using Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). From January 5 to March 5, 2026, we performed a prospective comparative evaluation. We randomised 202 participants (1:1) to usual care or artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted care, of whom 200 were analysed. We compared AI-assisted physician decision-making via an evolvable web-based online prediction platform versus usual care. The outcome was overall quality score of the final clinical recommendation. The platform supports follow-up data collection for future offline model updating. Findings In the training dataset, cure, recurrence, amputation, and all-cause mortality occurred in 638, 208, 226, and 167 patients, respectively; the corresponding numbers in the external validation dataset were 80, 34, 24, and 25. In independent external validation, the ST-XGBoost + ST-MLP ensemble outperformed six comparators, with a macro-averaged AUC of 0.901, accuracy of 0.875, and F1 score of 0.830. Outcome-specific discrimination was highest for amputation (AUC 0.953) and all-cause mortality (AUC 0.951), followed by cure (AUC 0.880) and recurrence (AUC 0.820). In the prospective evaluation, AI-assisted recommendations received higher scores than corresponding clinician recommendations (7.77 vs 6.47; mean difference 1.30, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.08–1.52; p < 0.0001), with the largest gain in completeness. The AI-assisted group showed better short-term follow-up engagement and glucose-management adherence. Interpretation We demonstrate that integrating gradient-boosted trees and neural networks enables explainable prediction of complex DFU trajectories and may support prioritised, individualised clinical decision-making. Nevertheless, recurrence estimates should be interpreted cautiously. Funding Xuzhou Municipal Health Commission Science and Technology Project (XWYHT20240128).

items.title: An explainable graph learning framework for carbon footprint prediction: Integrating SHAP-based policy insights and country similarity networks
items.abstract: Accurate prediction of carbon footprint dynamics is essential for climate policy design and sustainable development planning, yet complex nonlinear interactions among energy systems, environmental factors, and socioeconomic activities make estimation challenging. To address this gap, this study proposes an integrated framework combining machine learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and graph neural networks to predict carbon footprints across 27 European countries from 2015 to 2023. Evaluating several algorithms revealed that tree-based models substantially outperformed linear approaches, with LightGBM achieving the highest machine learning performance. SHAP analyses identified fossil fuel dependency, municipal waste generation, environmental impacts, protection capacity, and climate initiatives as the primary predictive determinants. Furthermore, incorporating a country similarity network into Graph Neural Network architectures improved predictive accuracy, with the Graph Attention Network (GAT) delivering the overall best predictive performance. Robustness checks confirmed model stability across various configurations, demonstrating that carbon footprint formation is driven by both national indicators and structural cross-country relationships. Ultimately, this framework bridges a methodological gap in environmental forecasting, offering robust predictive tools for policymakers and actionable, feature-level insights for targeted climate mitigation strategies.

items.title: ANÁLISE COMPARATIVA DE INTELIGÊNCIAS ARTIFICIAIS PARA PESQUISA E DESENVOLVIMENTO DE HISTÓRIAS E PERSONAGENS BASEADAS NO FOLCLORE BRASILEIRO
items.abstract: This research explores the potential of Brazilian folklore and literature as a source for audiovisual productions with global reach. Given the growing integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in academic and creative research, this study conducted a comparative analysis of four large language models (ChatGPT-4, Grok-3, DeepSeek v3, and Gemini 2.5). Methodologically, this is an applied, exploratory study with a qualitative approach, based on the collection and triangulation of data artificially generated through a standardized prompt. The results revealed that while the models consistently suggested popular figures such as Saci-Pererê and Iara, a prominent algorithmic bias toward Hollywood commercial patterns and cultural homogenization emerged. DeepSeek v3 showed greater ethnic-cultural diversity by including Indigenous and African myths , but all tools failed to access niche legends or oral traditions. It is concluded that, although AIs are valuable tools for complementing traditional folkloric research, they cannot replace it. In-depth human research remains essential to uncover the nuances and the vast range of lesser-known figures in Brazilian folklore, ensuring the authenticity and originality necessary for cultural and commercial success.

items.title: ANALISIS DAMPAK PENGGUNAAN APLIKASI SRIKANDI TERHADAP PRODUKTIVITAS PEGAWAI ADMINISTRASI DI MAN KOTA SURABAYA
items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengkaji implementasi aplikasi SRIKANDI (Sistem Informasi Kearsipan Dinamis Terintegrasi) terhadap produktivitas tenaga administrasi di Madrasah Aliyah Negeri (MAN) Kota Surabaya. Penelitian menggunakan metode kualitatif deskriptif dengan pengumpulan data melalui wawancara mendalam kepada tiga informan yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan representasi pengguna: Kepala Tata Usaha, tenaga administrasi senior, dan pegawai baru. Temuan penelitian memperlihatkan berdasarkan persepsi informan bahwa pemanfaatan aplikasi SRIKANDI berkontribusi dalam peningkatan efisiensi waktu kerja, penghematan biaya operasional, kemudahan dalam memantau kinerja berdasarkan data, serta percepatan penelusuran arsip. Namun demikian, implementasinya masih menghadapi sejumlah kendala yang dikategorikan ke dalam faktor manusia (human factor), faktor teknis (technical factor), dan faktor organisasi (organizational factor). Berdasarkan hasil penelitian tersebut, dapat disimpulkan bahwa keberhasilan transformasi administrasi digital tidak semata-mata ditentukan oleh kualitas teknologi, melainkan juga oleh kesiapan sumber daya manusia dan komitmen organisasi.

items.abstract: Perkembangan large language model (LLM) menimbulkan peluang sekaligus ketergantungan baru terhadap data, model, infrastruktur komputasi, dan mekanisme pengendalian yang berada di luar kendali organisasi atau negara pengguna. Artikel konseptual ini membahas strategi pembangunan kemampuan sovereign AI untuk konteks Indonesia melalui pembangunan dataset lokal dan adaptasi foundation model yang selaras dengan konteks budaya. Kerangka yang diusulkan terdiri atas lima lapisan, yaitu data sovereignty, model adaptation, cultural alignment, evaluation, dan deployment. Dataset lokal diposisikan sebagai aset pengetahuan yang memerlukan provenance, licensing, privacy, access control, dan governance. Adaptasi model memanfaatkan open foundation model melalui continued pre-training atau fine-tuning dengan pendekatan parameter-efficient seperti LoRA. Cultural alignment dirancang melalui preference data dan rubric lokal, sedangkan evaluasi diusulkan mencakup dimensi bahasa, budaya, hukum, safety, dan nilai. Artikel ini menegaskan bahwa sovereign AI tidak identik dengan isolasi teknologi atau pembangunan model dari nol. Kedaulatan dipahami sebagai kemampuan, governance, dan optionality untuk menentukan kapan teknologi global digunakan dan kapan capability yang lebih terkontrol diperlukan. Kerangka ini bersifat konseptual dan memerlukan validasi empiris pada tahap berikutnya. Kata kunci: sovereign AI; dataset lokal; foundation model; cultural alignment; data sovereignty

items.title: ANALISIS TINGKAT PENERIMAAN TEKNOLOGI ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE PADA MAHASISWA DAN MASYARAKAT
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is now widely used in academic and daily activities, yet its acceptance may differ across user groups. This study measures the level of AI acceptance among university students and the general public, examines the effect of perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness on behavioral intention, and tests differences between the two groups. A quantitative survey based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) was conducted with 49 respondents (30 students and 19 members of the public). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, path analysis, and the Mann–Whitney test. AI acceptance was high (M = 3,60). Perceived ease of use significantly affected perceived usefulness (β = 0,830) and behavioral intention (β = 0,448), whereas the effect of perceived usefulness on behavioral intention was not significant (β = 0,280). Behavioral intention positively affected daily AI use (β = 0,411) but explained only a small share of its variance (R² = 0,169). No significant differences were found between students and the public on any variable. The findings suggest that ease of use is the key to AI adoption, so simple interfaces and user training should be prioritised.

items.title: Analysing influence of usage patterns and reliance of artificial intelligence (AI) on learners critical thinking in higher institutions of learning
items.abstract: AI tools (ChatGPT, Grammarly, Gemini, QuillBot) are increasingly used in higher education to support learning and writing, but concerns exist about learner dependency and its impact on critical thinking and independent learning. This study examined the association between AI reliance and critical thinking among students from five Kenyan universities. Using a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design, data were collected from 275 students via questionnaires. Quantitative analysis included descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, regression, and ANOVA. Results showed moderate AI reliance for tasks such as assignment preparation and idea generation. A modest positive correlation was found between AI use and critical thinking (r=0.24, p < 0.05). Self-directed learning (β = 0.29) and purposeful AI use (β = 0.21) were significantly associated with critical thinking. ANOVA indicated that moderate AI users had higher critical thinking scores than those reporting low or excessive AI use.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Data Transmission over Telecommunication Networks
items.abstract: In modern and future telecommunication systems-particularly within 5G-Advanced and emerging 6G networks-data transmission optimization remains a critical challenge in the context of the terahertz (THz) spectrum, ultra-reliable lowlatency communications (URLLC), and massive Internet of Things (mMTC).Analytical models relying on traditional Shannon-Kotelnikov theory fall short in achieving fully efficient resource management and signal recovery under dynamic environments characterized by high fading, multipath propagation, and intense interference.This research provides a comprehensive analysis of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) algorithms across all stages of data transmission.It proposes a hybrid physicalstatistical framework that merges the mathematical models of the physical layer with data-driven ML methods based on Edge AI.As part of this study, a 5G HetNet topology comprising macrocells, pico-cells, and IoT nodes was simulated using NS-3 (Network Simulator 3).The performance of SVM, Decision Trees, K-means, and PCA was evaluated alongside reinforcement learning models (Q-learning, Deep Q-Networks -DQN).The obtained simulation results demonstrate that the hybrid ML approach, and specifically deep reinforcement learning (RL), enables reducing network latency by up to 22%, increasing overall throughput by 18%, raising the accuracy of anomaly and security attack detection to 94%, and significantly enhancing energy efficiency compared to traditional routing and resource allocation methods.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in Sports Performance Analysis
items.abstract: Abstract: AI is increasingly playing a significant role in sports today, and it's transforming the way athletes are evaluated, trained, and monitored. It enables coaches, sports scientists and athletes to explore vast quantities of performance data and find patterns that they might not otherwise be able to see through traditional methods. Technologies like machine learning, computer vision, wearable technology, predictive analytics, and automated video analysis are also being applied to a growing number of technical skills, physical performance, tactical movements, training workload, recovery and injury risk studies. Such technologies can deliver real-time and personalized data to coaches to create training plans based on the unique requirements of athletes and make informed decisions. AI can also aid in talent identification and performance prediction by integrating data collected from physical, physiological, biomechanical, and psychological factors. While these are advantages, there are also drawbacks to using AI in sports. Data quality, privacy, cost, technical, algorithmic bias and ethical considerations should be taken seriously. The article will explore the key applications of AI in sports performance analysis, as well as its potential benefits in enhancing athlete development and performance, and its current challenges and future prospects.

items.title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Detection and Prediction of Atrial Fibrillation in ECG Recordings – A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Introduction and purpose. Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia and a leading cause of ischaemic stroke, yet it frequently remains undiagnosed because of its paroxysmal and often asymptomatic nature. Artificial intelligence (AI), and in particular deep learning applied to the electrocardiogram (ECG), has emerged as a transformative approach both for detecting AF when the arrhythmia is present and for predicting future AF from an ECG recorded during sinus rhythm. The purpose of this narrative review is to summarise the current state of knowledge on AI-enabled ECG analysis for the detection and prediction of AF and to critically appraise its clinical readiness. Description of the state of knowledge. Convolutional neural networks can classify AF on single-lead and twelve-lead ECG with cardiologist-level accuracy (area under the curve, AUC, above 0.97 for rhythm classification) and can identify an "electrocardiographic signature" of AF on a normal sinus-rhythm tracing (AUC approximately 0.87). Consumer wearables using photoplethysmography and single-lead ECG achieve pooled sensitivity and specificity around 95%. Predictive models for incident AF reach AUC values of 0.78–0.85 and have been validated prospectively, enriching the diagnostic yield of screening. Nevertheless, false positives, unclassifiable tracings, limited external validity, and the absence of trials demonstrating a reduction in stroke temper enthusiasm. Summary. AI-ECG is a mature and accurate tool for AF detection and a promising instrument for AF prediction, but its translation into improved patient-relevant outcomes remains unproven. Rigorous external validation, outcome-driven randomised trials, and clear regulatory and implementation frameworks are required before routine clinical adoption. Keywords: Atrial Fibrillation; Artificial Intelligence; Deep Learning; Electrocardiography; Mass Screening; Stroke

items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Teaching, Learning, and Research
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly shaping teaching, learning, and research by offering tools that can support educational practice and academic work. This paper examines AI applications in education, their potential benefits, associated challenges, and ethical implications. It considers how AI can assist teachers with lesson planning, instructional materials, assessment, and feedback; support students through personalized learning and explanations of academic concepts; and help researchers with literature searches, data analysis, reference organization, and academic writing. Drawing on a review of existing literature, the paper identifies opportunities to improve educational efficiency, accessibility, and academic productivity. It also highlights concerns involving data privacy, algorithmic bias, inaccurate outputs, academic dishonesty, unequal access to technology, and overdependence on AI tools. The literature points to the importance of user training, ethical guidelines, institutional support, and critical evaluation of AI-generated content (Maphalala & Ajani, 2025; Khatri & Karki, 2023). The paper argues that AI should complement—not replace—teachers, learners, and researchers. Responsible integration requires a balance between technological innovation and human judgment, creativity, critical thinking, and academic integrity.

items.title: Artificial intelligence adoption and the term structure of corporate default risk
items.abstract: Purpose This paper provides evidence on whether corporate investment in artificial intelligence (AI) predicts corporate default risk, using the full term structure of forward-looking probabilities of default (PD). Design/methodology/approach Validated firm-level AI-investment measures built from employee resumes and job postings are merged with NUS-CRI forward-intensity PDs for U.S. listed non-financial firms (outcomes 2011–2018). Because PD is a fraction in [0,1], estimation uses fractional logit with industry and year fixed effects; identification is probed with a university AI-talent-supply instrument in a control-function design with bootstrap inference for the generated regressor, matching and entropy balancing and an extensive robustness battery. Findings A one-standard-deviation increase in AI investment is associated with significantly lower default probability at 12- to 36-month horizons – about 8 basis points at 12 months, roughly one-quarter of the sample mean. The relative effect declines with horizon and is concentrated within the first two years. A control-function test does not reject exogeneity, so the fractional-logit estimates are preferred, with the instrument as corroboration; results are robust to the job-posting measure, alternative industry classifications and screens and R&D and capital-intensity controls. Originality/value To our knowledge, the first firm-level evidence linking validated AI-investment measures to the PD term structure for U.S. listed firms, showing that labor-market footprints of AI adoption carry default-relevant information and that the association is a short-to-medium-horizon phenomenon.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Auditor Professional Judgement
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can assist audit analysis while changing how professionals evaluate evidence and accept advice. This systematic literature review examines the evidence supporting concerns about over-reliance on AI in audit decision-making. An OpenAlex title-and-abstract search and supplementary Consensus and SciSpace searches conducted on 29 October 2026 identified 149 records. After deduplication and eligibility assessment, 12 empirical journal studies were included. Five experimental reports, five surveys and two qualitative studies were synthesised using a design-sensitive approach and a six-domain critical appraisal. The experimental evidence more clearly demonstrates context-dependent advice-taking and algorithm aversion than the prevalence of inappropriate acceptance of incorrect AI advice. Survey associations between technology use, trust and reported scepticism do not establish behavioural calibration. Qualitative findings identify responsibility and professional learning as consequential organisational concerns. A proposed framework distinguishes output validity, trust, verification, reliance and defensible judgement, and generates four propositions for future testing. Practical implications include access to contradictory evidence, evaluation of both acceptance and rejection errors, and review that examines reasons for reliance. Limited search coverage, inaccessible reports, version differences, partial full-text access and an AI-assisted singleworkflow process constrain confidence. The review supports proportionate safeguards and better behavioural measurement without estimating a population rate of auditor over-reliance.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Didactics: Insights for teaching Latin
items.abstract: The article examines the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the didactics of Latin, framing AI as a transformative epistemic mediator rather than a mere technological adjunct. In the evolving digital landscape, AI is reshaping educational processes by influencing how knowledge is accessed, structured, and interpreted. The study critically explores four key areas—adaptive learning, gamification, assisted translation, and digital resources—demonstrating how AI can enhance pedagogical personalization, engagement, and inclusive learning experiences. Special attention is given to the challenges posed by algorithmic opacity, teacher mediation, and the ethical tensions surrounding automation in educational settings. The Latin language, understood as a symbolic and logical construct, is presented as uniquely suited to benefit from AI-enhanced learning environments, which can support complex interpretive practices. When implemented within a coherent pedagogical framework, critically and ethically, AI has the potential to revitalize classical language teaching, enhance students’ interpretive skills and metalinguistic skills, foster both critical literacy and meaningful interaction with classical texts. Ultimately, this contribution argues for a humanistic and ethically grounded approach on AI integration in education: Latin and AI together offer new avenues for promoting critical thinking and cultural awareness in education, reaffirming the relevance of classical studies in the digital age. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence; Inclusion; Teacher Education; Latin Didactics; Inclusive Technologies.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in Higher Education: A Systematic Review of Opportunities, Challenges and Emerging Trends
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence AI is getting more and more involved in higher education, it is reshaping teaching, learning , assessment, academic administration, research, and even how institutions decide things. In the last few years the fast rise of generative artificial intelligence GenAI, plus intelligent tutoring systems, learning analytics, automated assessment, recommendation systems, and AI assisted administrative tools has opened up new possibilities for universities, yet it also brings worries like academic integrity, data privacy, algorithmic bias, digital inequality, transparency, and changing professional roles. This paper actually uses a secondary-data based systematic review, looking at research and policy sources about AI and digital transformation in higher education. The review brings together outcomes from academic studies, other systematic reviews, and international policy frameworks, sort of to map out the main uses, opportunities, obstacles, and the kind of emerging trends that are starting to show up. What the literature suggests is that AI in education is not only about making content. It also includes adaptive learning, personalized tutoring, intelligent assessment, profiling and prediction, and support for institutional management. At the same time, good adoption does not just happen, it needs institutional policies, AI literacy, ethical safety nets, teacher professional development, careful responsible assessment approaches, and a human centered way of putting things into practice. A number of recent international frameworks stress human agency, ethics, AI competencies, and responsible usage, so there is a clear direction there. Overall the review shows that AI is best understood as augmentation tech with AI to help educators and learners not to flip a switch and replace the educational roles that already exist. For digital transformation a balance must exist, with technical novelty on one side and pedagogical sense together with ethical norms institutional realities and human factors, on the other. None of those should be treated as optional because leaving one out tends to break the system quickly.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications in Pharmaceutical Analysis: From Traditional Analytical Approaches to Intelligent Pharmaceutical Systems – A Comprehensive Review
items.abstract: Pharmaceutical analysis underpins the identity, purity, potency and safety of medicines. Conventional workflows based on chromatography, spectroscopy and mass spectrometry are reliable but depend on manual interpretation and generate data volumes that are hard to exploit fully. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer data-driven tools for peak detection, retention-time and spectral prediction, impurity identification, dissolution and stability modelling, anomaly detection and real-time process analytical technology (PAT). This narrative review, based on a structured search of peer-reviewed and regulatory sources published mainly from 2021 to 2026, compares traditional and AI-enabled workflows, summarises ML methods and their applications across analytical areas, and examines explainable AI, digital twins, generative AI and autonomous laboratories. In the sources reviewed, the strongest evidence concerns spectroscopy-based prediction for PAT and dissolution and retention-time prediction supported by large public datasets, whereas evidence for stability forecasting, rare-impurity identification and autonomous laboratories is limited and seldom validated at industrial scale. Regulatory thinking is converging on risk-based, context-of-use credibility assessment and lifecycle management. We propose a conceptual Intelligent Pharmaceutical Analysis Framework (IPAF) linking instrumentation, data integrity, AI analytics, decision support and governance, and identify priorities: standardised validated datasets, explainable and uncertainty-aware models, and prospective multi-site validation.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and the Internet of Things in Education: A Scientometric Mapping of Growth, Thematic Evolution, and Intellectual Structure in a Decade of Scopus-Indexed Research
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) has been advanced as the technical foundation of adaptive, sensor-rich learning environments, yet the structure and maturity of the resulting literature have not been mapped systematically. This study reports a scientometric analysis of 824 Scopus-indexed documents published between 2016 and 2025, retrieved with a TITLE-ABS-KEY query combining AI, IoT, and education and screened in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement. Performance analysis and science mapping were conducted with the bibliometrix R package (Biblioshiny) and VOSviewer, and comprised source, authorship, and country analyses, keyword co-occurrence, a strategic thematic map, thematic evolution across three periods, author co-citation, and a logistic life-cycle model. The corpus was produced by 2,668 authors across 525 sources, and annual output rose from a single document in 2016 to 274 in 2024. Publication is markedly dispersed: computing proceedings series and engineering outlets, rather than education journals, head the Bradford core; conference papers account for 47.1% of research documents; and author productivity departs sharply from Lotka’s law (β = 5.07), with 95.4% of authors contributing a single document. India and China dominate corresponding authorship, whereas international co-authorship remains modest at 20.87%. Artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things, and machine learning form a single central keyword cluster, while educational terms occupy peripheral clusters. The strategic map contains basic and niche themes but no motor theme, and thematic evolution shows continuous lineages for AI and IoT but none for pedagogy. Author co-citation reveals an intellectual base drawn from Industry 4.0, cyber-physical systems, and machine-learning research, with education-specific authors at its periphery. A logistic model signaled saturation (K = 869), but sensitivity analyses showed this to be an artifact of the partial 2025 year; on complete or annualized data, the field is at or just before its inflection point. The field is therefore expanding but unconsolidated, technologically driven, and reliant on an intellectual base imported from outside education. Implications for research agendas, publication strategy, and capacity building are discussed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Transformations in the Labour Market
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is one of the most significant technological developments of the 21st century, and it is impacting the global job market in profound ways. AI-powered tools like machine learning, robotics, natural language processing, and automation have transformed the nature of work, the productivity of industries and countries, and the skills that the workforce needs in developed and developing countries. This research paper analyses change in employment, job displacement, skill transformation, productivity increases, wage inequality, and labour market polarization caused by the impact of AI on the global labour market. The study also explores changes in manufacturing, healthcare, financial services, retail, logistics, education and information technology by sector. This study is qualitative and quantitative, based on secondary data obtained from international organizations like the International Labour Organization (ILO), the World Economic Forum (WEF), the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and the World Bank (WB). The analysis of the data from 2018 to 2025 will provide insights into the evolving employment landscape as a result of AI adoption. The study highlights the potential of AI to boost productivity, efficiency, and economic growth, as well as the challenges it poses, such as job displacement, technological unemployment, growing income inequality, and skill mismatches. The results indicate that repetitive and routine occupations are most likely to be automated, while creative, emotionally intelligent, and advanced analytical jobs grow. The paper also delves into the new roles in data science, AI engineering, cybersecurity, digital marketing, and human-machine collaboration. The developing countries have different challenges because of poor digital infrastructure, low technological readiness and inadequate training of the workforce. Developed economies, on the other hand, have the better option to adapt via innovation ecosystems and skill development programs. The study emphasizes the importance of governments, educational institutions, multinational corporations, and international organizations to make working life easier for people with disabilities to transition into and out of. The paper argues that AI does not only pose a threat, and is not an automatic assurance of economic well-being, but rather the impact of AI relies on policy response, workforce adaptability and technological ethical governance. Therefore, public policies to promote reskilling and lifelong learning, labour protection, digital inclusion and social security systems are required to ensure the sustainability of employment in the face of technology. The study suggests a collective global governance approach to ensure equitable distribution of the opportunities of AI-enabled economic transformation across societies and labour markets globally. The objectives, as well as the concepts of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Lay of the Land – Labour Market, Employment Trends, Job Displacement, AI's contribution to GDP growth, Workforce Transformation and Digital Skills and Policy recommendations, will be addressed.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Climate Change Prediction
items.abstract: Abstract Climate change presents a growing danger to ecosystems, infrastructure, and human safety, heightening the need for prediction systems that are both precise and rapid enough to facilitate prompt decision-making. Artificial intelligence (AI), especially deep learning, has arisen as a revolutionary enhancement to conventional physics-based numerical models. This manuscript examines the application of AI methodologies, such as graph neural networks, transformers, Fourier neural operators, and ensemble deep-learning frameworks, throughout the climate-prediction continuum, encompassing short-term weather forecasting to multi-decadal climate model simulation, sea-level forecasting, and greenhouse gas emission estimation. We encapsulate notable systems documented in contemporary literature, examine the computational and scientific benefits that AI presents in comparison to traditional numerical weather prediction (NWP), and delineate the key obstacles, such as data insufficiency, physical coherence, interpretability, and energy expenditure, that need resolution prior to the reliable implementation of AI-driven climate forecasting at an operational level. We finish with guidance on hybrid physics-AI modelling as a means to get dependable, practical climate insights.

items.abstract: This report presents a literature review and discussion focused on the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support future flight operations, particularly within the context of Single Pilot Operations (SPO) and failure mitigation. items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Institutional Accreditation in India: A Framework for NAAC's Data-Driven Quality Assurance
items.abstract: Abstract For nearly three decades, the National Assessment and Accreditation Council (NAAC) has been India's main mechanism for assuring quality in higher education. Its traditional model — built around a self-reported Self-Study Report, a data validation stage, and an on-site peer-team visit ending in a letter grade — has come under increasing strain. Critics point to slow turnaround, difficulty in standardizing judgments across assessor teams, and the challenge of scaling the process to the thousands of institutions India now wishes to bring under formal quality review. In February 2025, NAAC announced a major reform: a binary accreditation outcome, an optional five-level Maturity-Based Graded Level (MBGL) scale for institutions seeking continuous improvement, a unified national data platform, and the beginnings of an AI-assisted evaluation engine to reduce the burden of manual verification. This paper builds on that reform and proposes, in concrete technical terms, what such an AI-assisted engine could look like. We outline a system that can read and structure Self-Study Reports, cross-check institutional claims against government data sources such as UGC, AICTE, AISHE and NIRF, benchmark institutions against their peers, and present the results to human assessors without replacing their judgment. The discussion is grounded in India's higher-education context: wide variation in digital readiness across institutions, obligations under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the well-known risk that metric-driven systems can encourage institutions to "write to the metric" rather than improve underlying quality. We conclude with a phased pilot study to test the framework before any wider rollout.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in adaptive radiotherapy for head and neck cancer: a systematic review of synthetic CT, automated segmentation and prediction of anatomical change and adaptive RT requirement
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored to overcome the technical and workflow challenges of adaptive radiotherapy (ART) in head and neck cancer (HNC). However, the available evidence remains heterogeneous, with varying degrees of technical and clinical validation. This review evaluated the current role and clinical maturity of AI-enabled ART in HNC. A systematic literature search of PubMed, Scopus and EMBASE was performed from inception to 1 August 2026. Original prospective or retrospective human studies published between 1 January 2020 and 1 August 2026 were eligible. Studies were restricted to photon-based radiotherapy using CBCT, kVCT or MVCT. Eligible studies were classified into four domains: synthetic CT/image enhancement; AI-based auto-segmentation and deformable image registration; anatomical change prediction and adaptive planning; and prediction of ART requirement. Reporting quality was assessed using CLAIM 2024, QUADAS-2 was applied where appropriate. Out of 62 records screened, 25 studies were included. Sixteen studies addressed synthetic CT/image enhancement, seven addressed auto-segmentation/deformable registration, two evaluated anatomical change prediction/adaptive planning, and three investigated predictions of ART requirement, with some overlap between domains. AI consistently demonstrated technical improvements in image quality, CT-number accuracy, segmentation performance and dosimetric agreement. However, evidence for prospective prediction of anatomical change and ART requirement was considerably limited. CLAIM adherence ranged from approximately 68% to 88%, with a mean of 79.9%±5.8%. AI demonstrates substantial technical potential across HNC ART workflows, particularly for image synthesis, segmentation and registration. However, multicentre evidence demonstrating improved clinical decision-making and patient outcomes remains insufficient.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN AQUACULTURE: APPLICATIONS, RESEARCH GAPS, AND IMPLICATIONS FOR PROFESSIONAL EDUCATION AND GOVERNANCE — A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in aquaculture to support monitoring, prediction, automation, and production management, while also creating new requirements for professional competence, ethical oversight, and governance. This systematic literature review, conducted under an integrative approach and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020, examined practical applications of AI and their implications for professional education and governance in aquaculture. Searches in Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar identified 877 records, of which 97 met the eligibility criteria and were included in the qualitative synthesis. The evidence was concentrated on technical applications, particularly fish detection and biomass estimation, water and environmental monitoring, automated production systems, health and biosecurity, and feeding and growth optimization. Direct educational evidence was scarce: only one study examined aquaculture professionals' knowledge and interest in AI, and no included study evaluated formal curricular interventions or learning outcomes in Fisheries Engineering. The synthesis also identified concerns involving data quality, algorithmic bias, technological exclusion, privacy, standardization, and accountability. These findings indicate that responsible adoption requires locally representative data, transparent validation, digital and data literacy, human oversight, and coordinated governance. AI has substantial potential to support aquaculture, but its contribution to professional education remains an important and insufficiently investigated research field.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in axial spondyloarthritis imaging: a review of current evidence
items.abstract: The diagnosis of axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) remains challenging and is frequently delayed. Imaging is central to diagnosis, but relevant inflammatory and structural abnormalities may be subtle, heterogeneous, or overlap with findings related to mechanical stress, anatomical variation, and degeneration. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning, is therefore being investigated to support image interpretation, lesion detection, quantification, and standardized assessment. We synthesize evidence from 12 studies applying convolutional neural networks and related architectures to magnetic resonance imaging and radiographs, automate imaging scores, and combine imaging-derived information with clinical variables. Several models achieved performance comparable to experienced human readers, including during external validation. However, performance may decline in heterogeneous real-world populations for study-specific reasons not explained solely by scanner or protocol differences. No AI tool currently has regulatory clearance for autonomous use in axSpA, and applications remain largely confined to research and clinical trials.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in FDA regulatory correspondence, 2022 to 2026: a retrospective document analysis
items.abstract: This review measured how often, and in what context, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) refers to artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI, in warning letters. A search was conducted of the full text of all FDA warning letters issued from January 1, 2022, through September 28, 2026, taken from FDA’s public warning letter database. The search terms were “artificial intelligence,” “AI,” “machine learning,” and 4 related terms. Every letter containing a term was assessed and read in full, and the violations cited in each included letter were counted. Form FDA 483s and establishment inspection reports (EIRs) that refer to AI were described separately. Of 3,011 warning letters, 7 (0.23%) referred to AI: 3 device, 3 tobacco, and 1 drug letter. Only the April 2026 letter to Purolea Cosmetics Lab treated a firm’s use of AI as a violation, citing unreviewed AI-generated documents under 21 CFR 211.22(c). In addition, 1 EIR and 2 Form 483s referred to AI. FDA references to AI in warning letters are rare, recent, and heterogeneous, and most describe AI-enabled products subject to existing authorization requirements. The Purolea letter shows that FDA will cite unreviewed AI output under existing current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) rules.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN JUDICIAL SYSTEMS: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF REGULATORY READINESS AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN INDONESIA, SINGAPORE AND UGANDA
items.abstract: Increasingly, Artificial Intelligence (AI) is influencing the way courts operate. However, there are significant differences regarding the integration and regulation of the use of AI in various jurisdictions. While most studies have thus far concentrated mainly on issues related to ethics and country-specific national AI strategies, existing literature has paid relatively little attention to what regulatory conditions must exist prior to and subsequent to the introduction of AI technology within the court system. This article examines regulatory preparedness and accountability in a comparative analysis of Indonesia, Singapore and Uganda. These three countries are at significantly varying levels of digitalization in their judicial processes. Using both a doctrine-based and comparative method, this article assesses legislative and policy frameworks, institutional capabilities, digital infrastructure, judicial oversight, transparency, explanations and procedural protections. The study contributes to judicial AI governance scholarship by showing, through a comparative analysis, that judicial digitalisation alone does not establish regulatory readiness for AI and that regulatory readiness and accountability must develop together rather than in sequence. An effective AI-enabled justice governance system requires appropriate legal and institutional frameworks that protect judicial independence, procedural fairness, and meaningful human oversight, while also allowing for technologically innovative solutions that are consistent with the rule of law.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Smart Cities: Intelligent Solutions, Applications, Challenges, and Emerging Research Trends
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as an important technology for developing smart cities by improving urban services, resource management, public transportation, energy efficiency, environmental monitoring, and citizen services. The increasing population of urban areas creates challenges related to traffic congestion, pollution, waste management, electricity consumption, and efficient public administration. Traditional city management systems often depend on manual monitoring and separate information systems, which can limit real-time decision-making and coordination. This paper presents a structured review of AI applications in smart cities and proposes an integrated AI-based framework for intelligent urban management. The proposed framework combines the Internet of Things (IoT), machine learning, data analytics, cloud computing, and intelligent decision-support mechanisms to collect, process, and analyze urban data. It focuses on traffic management, smart energy systems, waste collection, environmental monitoring, and citizen services. The paper also discusses the benefits, implementation challenges, limitations, and future research opportunities associated with AI-enabled urban development. Existing research indicates that AI can support more efficient and responsive city services; however, data privacy, cybersecurity, infrastructure costs, interoperability, algorithmic bias, and digital inclusion remain important concerns. The proposed framework provides a conceptual foundation for developing sustainable, intelligent, and citizen-centered smart cities.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Teaching and Governance in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) Schools: Basis for Framework Development
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) adoption in schools creates opportunities for instructional innovation but also raises questions concerning governance, professional judgement, and institutional readiness. This study examined AI integration and governance in selected United Arab Emirates (UAE) schools and developed a leadership-guided implementation framework. An exploratory sequential mixed-methods design combined semi-structured interviews with 10 purposively selected teachers and school leaders and a subsequent structured survey of 80 respondents, selected through stratified sampling. Interview transcripts underwent thematic analysis; quantitative responses were analysed using weighted means, standard deviations, and Pearson product–moment correlations at the .05 significance level. Seven qualitative themes clustered into AI integration and AI governance. Overall AI integration was rated moderate (grand weighted mean [GWM] = 3.41), with adaptive integration highest (3.76), followed by professional productivity (3.38) and AI-enhanced teaching (3.08). Overall AI governance was high (GWM = 3.32), led by ethical governance (3.66), followed by strategic governance (3.34), organisational support (3.34), and uneven governance (2.97). Organisational support was significantly associated with all three AI-integration dimensions, while adaptive integration had its strongest observed association with ethical governance (r = .539, p < .001). Integrated findings informed the proposed Leadership-Guided AI Integration and Governance Framework for UAE Schools, emphasising pedagogical use, human oversight, ethical safeguards, strategic leadership, professional learning, and institutional readiness. The proposed framework is a study-derived practical output, not a causally validated model.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Telemedicine: Transforming Diagnosis and Personalized Care in Virtual Health Systems
items.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) within telemedicine has revolutionized virtual healthcare delivery by enabling high-precision diagnostics and tailored treatment strategies remotely. This paper evaluates state-of-the-art AI models applied to medical imaging and clinical text data within telehealth platforms, highlighting significant improvements in diagnostic accuracy and clinical decision support. Using deep learning architectures like ResNet-50 for imaging and BERT for natural language processing of electronic health records, the framework demonstrates enhanced patient care personalization and operational efficiency. Survey feedback from clinicians and patients underscores AI's practical benefits in improving healthcare accessibility and quality in remote settings. Challenges, including algorithmic biases and data privacy risks, are discussed, along with future research directions aimed at sustaining AI-driven telemedicine enhancements to health systems worldwide.

items.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE-GENERATED FEEDBACK VERSUS HUMAN FEEDBACK IN MEDICAL EDUCATION: AN INTEGRATIVE LITERATURE REVIEW
items.abstract: Introduction: Feedback is central to medical education, and generative artificial intelligence (AI) has made individualized, timely, and scalable feedback possible. Questions remain, however, about its accuracy, contextual relevance, and capacity to promote learning compared with feedback from faculty and clinical supervisors. Objective: To analyze the evidence on AI-generated feedback compared with human feedback in medical education, considering its quality, educational effectiveness, applicability, and limitations. Methods: Integrative review structured with the PICo strategy. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and LILACS were searched for studies published between January 2020 and October 2026 in English, Portuguese, or Spanish. Studies were classified by level of evidence, and findings were synthesized through interpretive thematic analysis. Results: Eleven studies from Canada, the United States, Germany, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, and Japan were included: five randomized trials (level II) and six comparative descriptive or mixed-methods studies (level VI). AI-generated feedback generally matched or exceeded human feedback in comprehensiveness, consistency, and adherence to predefined criteria, especially in written, structured, and simulated tasks. Human feedback was superior in clarity, relevance, and accuracy in some studies and in more complex diagnostic and therapeutic situations. Learning outcomes were measured only in the short term, and hybrid models combining AI data with faculty input showed favorable results. Conclusion: AI can increase the availability and consistency of feedback but does not replace the clinical and pedagogical judgment of faculty. Supervised integration of both modalities is the most consistent approach, and studies with longer-term outcomes and Latin American settings are needed.
